  WHY: _sanitize_bash_command returns the display text with the credential unmasked because the credential value was never added to the values set. The shape similarly retains the full token including the credential since _segment_shape does not recognize it as a -c command line either.

Without fish in the set, _segment_credentials line 535's any() check fails, the -c block is not entered, and the credential value is not extracted.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: Line or code reference: lines 244, 415-420, 533-543 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Attached command strings passed to shell -c flags without whitespace (such as sh -c'mysql -pSecret' or bash -c"curl -u user:pass") fail _SHELL_COMMAND_FLAG_RE matching in _segment_credentials and bypass attached-value cutting in _segment_shape, causing raw credentials to be leaked in both sanitized command output and the reported command shape.
  WHY: The regex _SHELL_COMMAND_FLAG_RE = re.compile(r"^(-[A-Za-z]*c|--(session-)?command)$") terminates with an end-of-string anchor ($), so tokens like -cmysql -pSecret produced by shlex when quotes directly touch -c do not match. Consequently, _command_line_credentials is never called to extract or mask the inner command line credentials in _segment_credentials, and _segment_shape treats the entire token as an uncut flag, posting the raw secret in the command shape and issue title.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: Line or code reference: lines 236-240, 305-327, 520-565 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py file modified in this PR retains an obsolete and vulnerable wrapper implementation (_COMMAND_WRAPPERS) that lacks shell -c command line parsing and omits wrappers like su, runuser, docker, and kubectl.
  WHY: Production environments invoke .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py. When commands use runuser, su, docker exec, or shell -c (e.g., runuser -u postgres -- mysql -pSecret or su -c 'mysql -pSecret'), the root script fails to identify the wrapped command or parse the inner command line, leaking raw credentials into ai:permission-prompt issue bodies and PR comments.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py: Line or code reference: lines 184 and 249 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: URL userinfo pattern [^\s/'\"]+@ in REDACTION_PATTERNS and _URL_USERINFO_RE does not stop at query string (?) or fragment (#) delimiters when matching URLs that lack a trailing path slash.
  WHY: For URLs without a path slash where query parameters or fragments contain an @ character (e.g., https://example.com?email=test@example.com or https://example.com#user@anchor), the greedy character class [^\s/'\"]+ matches past ? and # up to the @, replacing the entire hostname and parameter key with ***@ (e.g. producing https://***@example.com). Under RFC 3986 §3.2.1, userinfo is strictly part of the URI authority and is terminated by /, ?, or #.
